# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Skyler Brooks**
Member ID: W708133981
[Street Address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-06 — Reference number POC-7572D3C32F-37314**
**Member:** Skyler Brooks | **Member ID:** W708133981
**Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Texas
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which Aetna denied on 2026-08-06 under reference number POC-7572D3C32F-37314. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the records already in my file line up with the criteria Aetna itself publishes in CPB 0660, including the imaging criterion. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I set out the plan's own language and the matching evidence from my chart.

## 1. The imaging criterion — the reason given for the denial

The policy states:

> "Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) (see Appendix ) affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint; and"

My imaging study dated 2026-06-02 is an MRI of the knee. It reports full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and it grades my osteoarthritis as **Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially**. That is the exact grade the policy names, in a single compartment, as the policy describes. The findings are in the file that was reviewed.

If the denial rests on the type of study rather than on the findings, I would ask Aetna to say so plainly, and to identify what additional imaging it requires, so that my surgeon and I can respond. I am also willing to obtain any further imaging the plan specifies.

## 2. Pain and functional disability

> "Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint; and"

My records document 12 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3 to 4 times a night because of the pain.

## 3. Physical examination findings

> "Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination: and"

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. This excerpt ends in a colon and introduces a list that I was not given, so I cannot address any further detail it may contain. I ask Aetna to identify the specific list items it applied.

## 4. Arc of motion

> "Patient's knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less; and"

My records state that my range of motion is limited by pain, but the summary I have does not include a measurement in degrees. I ask that Aetna request the goniometric measurement from Dr. Lindqvist's office, or allow me to submit it, rather than treat a missing number as a failure to meet this criterion. [Insert measured arc of motion in degrees, if available from the chart.]

## 5. Unsuccessful conservative therapy

> "History of of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record (see Note Footnote3 *** ) with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy)."

I completed **16 weeks** of supervised physical therapy with a licensed physical therapist, from 2026-03-09 to 2026-06-29, with **16 visits completed**, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. All of it was formal, supervised, in-person therapy — not home or virtual — so the "at least half" requirement is exceeded. My BMI is 29 and my age is [insert date of birth / age]; the policy ties the 12- or 24-week figure to age and BMI, and I ask Aetna to state which duration it applied to me.

> "Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."

My therapy is documented in the physical therapy **discharge note**, which is in the packet. If an additional copy is needed, I will provide it on request.

The policy also lists these components of conservative management:

> "Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and"

I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.

> "Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; and"

My physical therapy was specifically directed at quadriceps strengthening and range of motion.

> "Supervised physical therapy (activities of daily living [ADLs] diminished despite completing a plan of care); and"

I completed the full 16-visit plan of care and my daily function remains diminished: I still cannot climb stairs without assistance and I still wake 3 to 4 times nightly with pain.

> "Activity modification; and"

[Insert any activity modification documented in the chart, if recorded.]

> "Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote4 † to joint replacement, optional for others); and"

My records state that I cannot climb stairs without assistance. [Insert any assistive device documented in the chart, if recorded.]

> "Therapeutic injections into the knee (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote4 † to joint replacement, optional for others)."

I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-08, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.

The policy also recognizes:

> "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral); and"

My MRI describes bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment. I completed the conservative course regardless, and it did not relieve my symptoms.

## 6. Ligaments, comorbidities, and HbA1c

> "Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament; and"

[Insert the ligament / ACL examination finding from Dr. Lindqvist's note.] This detail is not in the summary I have, and I ask that it be requested from my surgeon rather than assumed against me.

> "For members with significant conditions or co-morbidities, the risk/benefit of unicompartmental knee arthroplasty should be appropriately addressed in the medical record."

My records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

> "If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to knee arthroplasty."

[Confirm diabetes status; if diabetic, insert most recent HbA1c value and date.]

## What I am asking for

Please overturn the denial of CPT 27446 and authorize the partial knee replacement my surgeon has documented as medically necessary. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I ask Aetna to tell me in writing:

1. Which specific criterion or criteria in CPB 0660 my records were found not to meet;
2. What the plan considers acceptable imaging for the radiographic criterion, given that my MRI reports Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 in the medial compartment; and
3. Which conservative-therapy duration (12 or 24 weeks) was applied to me and why.

I would also like a copy of the clinical review criteria used in this determination, and I request review by a physician with orthopedic expertise. If any additional records would help, please contact me or Dr. Lindqvist's office and we will send them promptly.

My appeal must be received by **2027-02-02**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting this appeal with Aetna's **Member Complaint and Appeal Form**, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, by fax to **859-425-3379** or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I have confirmed before sending. I can also be reached by phone at the number below, and Aetna's member line is 1-800-872-3862.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I appreciate your time and your careful review of the records.

Sincerely,

**Skyler Brooks**
Member ID: W708133981
Reference number: POC-7572D3C32F-37314
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-03-09 to 2026-06-29] · [MRI report, 2026-06-02] · [Office notes from Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery] · [Injection record, 2026-04-08] · [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-06] · [Aetna Member Complaint and Appeal Form]
